discussionQuestions: Where do you tend to see shortage before you see God's provision?
What has God already placed in your hands that you may be overlooking?
What would surrender look like for you this week?
Why do you think the disciples' hearts were hardened even after the miracle of the loaves?
author: ROLCC Fellowship Team

sections.heading: Overview
sections.body:
Mark 6:35-44
MARK 6 : 33 But the multitudes saw them departing, and many knew Him and ran
there on foot from all the cities. They arrived before them and came together to Him.
34 And Jesus, when He came out, saw a great multitude and was moved with
compassion for them, because they were like sheep not having a shepherd. So He
began to teach them many things. 35 When the day was now far spent, His disciples
came to Him and said, “This is a deserted place, and already the hour is late. 36 Send
them away, that they may go into the surrounding country and villages and buy
themselves [g]bread; for they have nothing to eat.”

sections.heading: 1 THE DISCIPLES SAW A PROBLEM
sections.body:
Mark 6:35–36
“When the day was now far spent, His disciples came to Him and said, ‘This is a deserted
place, and already the hour is late. Send them away…’”
The disciples saw the lack of food
The disciples saw the difficulty
The disciples wanted to send the crowd away
Teaching:
● Human wisdom focuses on limitations
● We often see problems before possibilities
God sees provision where we see shortage.

sections.heading: 2 JESUS GAVE A CHALLENGE
sections.body:
Mark 6:37
“But He answered and said to them, ‘You give them something to eat.’ And they said to Him,
‘Shall we go and buy two hundred denarii worth of bread and give them something to eat?’”
Jesus challenged the disciples
The disciples calculated the cost
The disciples focused on what they lacked
Teaching:
● Jesus often stretches our faith
● God asks us to trust Him beyond our resources
Faith begins where human ability ends.

Mark 6:35-44

sections.heading: 3 JESUS ASKED WHAT THEY HAD
sections.body:
Mark 6:38
“But He said to them, ‘How many loaves do you have? Go and see.’ And when they found
out they said, ‘Five, and two fish.’”
Jesus did not ask what they lacked
Jesus asked what they had
The disciples found five loaves and two fish
Teaching:
● God starts with what is available
● Small resources in God’s hands become sufficient
God is not looking for abundance; He is looking for surrender.

sections.heading: 4 JESUS BROUGHT ORDER
sections.body:
Mark 6:39–40
“Then He commanded them to make them all sit down in groups on the green grass. So they
sat down in ranks, in hundreds and in fifties.”
Jesus organized the crowd
The people obeyed His instructions
Teaching:
● God is a God of order
● Preparation often comes before provision
Obedience prepares the way for miracles.

sections.heading: 5 JESUS BLESSED WHAT WAS
sections.body:
GIVEN

Mark 6:35-44
Mark 6:41
“And when He had taken the five loaves and the two fish, He looked up to heaven, blessed
and broke the loaves, and gave them to His disciples to set before them; and the two fish He
divided among them all.”
Jesus took the little they had
Jesus blessed it
Jesus broke it
Jesus gave it to the disciples
Teaching:
● What is blessed by God becomes fruitful
● God often multiplies what is surrendered
Blessing comes before multiplication.

sections.heading: 6 EVERYONE WAS FED
sections.body:
Mark 6:42
“So they all ate and were filled.”
Nobody went hungry
Everyone received enough
Teaching:
● God’s provision is sufficient
● Jesus cares about physical and spiritual needs
God is able to satisfy every need.

sections.heading: 7 THERE WAS LEFTOVER
sections.body:
Mark 6:43
“And they took up twelve baskets full of fragments and of the fish.”
Twelve baskets remained
God provided more than enough
Teaching:

Mark 6:35-44
● God is not limited by scarcity
● God’s provision overflows
With God there is abundance, not merely survival.

sections.heading: 8 THE SIZE OF THE MIRACLE
sections.body:
Mark 6:44
“Now those who had eaten the loaves were about five thousand men.”
About 5,000 men were fed
Including women and children, the crowd may have been much larger
Teaching:
● Nothing is impossible for Jesus
● The size of the need does not limit God’s power
Great needs create opportunities for great miracles.

sections.heading: JESUS WALKS ON THE SEA
sections.body:
Mark 6:48–51
After feeding the multitude, Jesus sent the disciples ahead in a boat.
A storm arose on the sea.
Jesus came walking on the water.
The disciples were terrified and thought they saw a ghost.
Jesus said:

Mark 6:35-44
Mark 6:50
"Be of good cheer! It is I; do not be afraid."
Jesus entered the boat and the wind ceased.

sections.heading: WHY WERE THE DISCIPLES SO AMAZED?
sections.body:
Mark 6:52
"For they had not understood about the loaves, because their heart was hardened."

quiz.question: What did the disciples want to do when evening came?
options: Send the crowd away to buy food
Leave Jesus and return to Capernaum
quiz.explanation: They saw only lack in a deserted place.

quiz.question: How many loaves and fish did the disciples find?
quiz.explanation: Jesus started with what they had.

quiz.question: What did Jesus do before the food was distributed?
options: He told the disciples to fast
He blessed and broke the loaves
He bought bread from a village

quiz.question: How much food was left after everyone ate?
Why were the disciples amazed on the sea (Mark 6:52)?
options: They refused to enter the boat
They had not understood about the loaves
quiz.explanation: Their hearts were hardened to the lesson of the miracle.

title: Mark 6:35-44 — Five Loaves and Two Fish
description: A cell fellowship study on Jesus feeding the five thousand — how God sees provision where we see shortage.

passageReading.text:
35 When the day was now far spent, His disciples came to Him and said, "This is a deserted place, and already the hour is late.
36 Send them away, that they may go into the surrounding country and villages and buy themselves bread; for they have nothing to eat."
37 But He answered and said to them, "You give them something to eat." And they said to Him, "Shall we go and buy two hundred denarii worth of bread and give them something to eat?"
38 But He said to them, "How many loaves do you have? Go and see." And when they found out they said, "Five, and two fish."
39 Then He commanded them to make them all sit down in groups on the green grass.
40 So they sat down in ranks, in hundreds and in fifties.
41 And when He had taken the five loaves and the two fish, He looked up to heaven, blessed and broke the loaves, and gave them to His disciples to set before them; and the two fish He divided among them all.
